text: Early in the morning Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) and all his troops camped beside the spring of Harod; the camp of Midian was north of them, near the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
The LORD said to Gideon, You have too many troops for me to hand Midian over to them, or Israel might boast against me, saying, My own strength saved me.
Now announce to the troops: Whoever is afraid or trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead. So twenty-two thousand went home, and ten thousand remained.
The LORD said to Gideon, There are still too many. Take them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. Whomever I say goes with you will go, and whomever I say does not go will not go.
So he took the troops down to the water, and the LORD told Gideon, Separate everyone who laps the water with his tongue like a dog from everyone who kneels down to drink.
The number who lapped with their hands to their mouths was three hundred; the rest of the troops knelt down to drink.
The LORD told Gideon, With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and hand Midian over to you; let everyone else go home.
So the men took provisions and their trumpets, and Gideon sent the rest of the Israelites back to their tents, keeping only the three hundred. The Midianite camp lay below him in the valley.
That night the LORD said to Gideon, Get up, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
But if you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp first with your servant Purah,
and listen to what they are saying; after that your hands will be strengthened to attack. So he went down with Purah to the outskirts of the armed men in the camp.
Midian, Amalek, and all the people of the east were spread out in the valley like locusts, and their camels were as numerous as sand on the seashore.

When Gideon arrived, a man was telling a friend about a dream: I dreamed that a loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the Midianite camp, struck a tent, and the tent collapsed and turned upside down.
His friend answered, This can only be the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite; God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hand.
When Gideon heard the dream and its interpretation, he bowed in worship, returned to the camp of Israel, and said, Get up! The LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hand.
He divided the three hundred men into three companies and put trumpets and empty jars with torches inside them into all their hands.
Watch me, he told them, and do as I do. When I get to the edge of the camp, do exactly as I do.
When I and everyone with me blow our trumpets, you also blow your trumpets all around the camp and shout, For the LORD and for Gideon!

Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after they had changed the guards; they blew the trumpets and smashed the jars in their hands.
The three companies blew their trumpets and shattered their jars; they held the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right, and they shouted, A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!
Each man stood in his place around the camp, and the whole camp ran, crying out as they fled.

When the three hundred trumpets sounded, the LORD caused the men throughout the camp to turn their swords against each other; the army fled toward Beth-shittah, toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.
Israelites from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh were called out, and they pursued Midian.

Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying, Come down against Midian and take control of the waters ahead of them, as far as Beth-barah, and also the Jordan. So all the men of Ephraim gathered and seized the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.

They captured two Midianite commanders, Oreb and Zeeb; they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb, and continued pursuing Midian, bringing the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
